findings.title: XSum AI-generated data and prompt file absent; neither documented run executes
findings.claim: For the paper's default (dataset_name=xsum, ai_source=llama2, token_size=200) the black-box run loads `./txtdata/xsum_from_ai_llama2_200.json`, and the white-box run additionally calls get_prompts→`./txtdata/xsum_prompt.json` (detector.py:1021); `txtdata/` ships only xsum_human.json, HC3_{ai,human,prompt}.json, writingprompts_{human,prompt}.json — the two XSum files are absent.
findings.concern: XSum is the paper's only dataset (Table 2/3/4); with the AI-generated summaries and the prompt file missing, `python detection.py` and `python detection.py --prompt` both fail with FileNotFoundError, so the headline results cannot be reproduced from the repo, and regenerating requires gated Llama-2-7b-chat access plus network.
findings.resolution: Ship xsum_from_ai_llama2_200.json and xsum_prompt.json (the exact 200+200 samples behind Table 2), or provide a resolvable, network-only fetch that does not depend on gated weights.
findings.reason: detection.py:30-33 quote matches exactly; defaults (xsum/llama2/200) confirmed at detection.py:85-89; xsum_from_ai_llama2_200.json and xsum_prompt.json (loaded at detector.py:1021) both confirmed absent from txtdata/ (only xsum_human.json, HC3_*, writingprompts_* present) via check_data_present.py.

findings.title: Tables 3–4 substitution-rate/sample-size sweeps have no driver script or outputs
findings.quote:
python detection.py # black-box detection
python detection.py --prompt # white-box detection
python detection.py --binoculars_only # black-box detection
python detection.py --binoculars_only  --prompt # white-box detection
findings.claim: The documented reproduction driver runs a single fixed configuration (default perturbation_num=5, pct_words_num=0.1, and one fast_sample_num) and never varies substitution rate or sample size; results/ contains only that one config; no script emits the SR∈{10,20,30,100}% × SS∈{5,10,10000} grid of Tables 3–4.
findings.concern: The Table 3–4 rows (the paper's sample-size/substitution-rate robustness claim for the Fast series) trace to no computing script and no committed output, so those numbers cannot be checked or regenerated without reverse-engineering the argument grid.
findings.resolution: Add a sweep driver (or a documented list of exact commands) that produces every Table 3 and Table 4 row, and commit the resulting output JSONs.
findings.reason: detection_all.sh:1-4 quote matches exactly; paper_text.txt confirms Table 3/4 use an SR/SS grid (10/20/30/100% x 5/10/10000); repo-wide grep shows perturbation_num/pct_words_num defaults (5, 0.1) are hardcoded everywhere with no sweep flag or driver script, and results/ contains only the single pn5_fpn10000_pwm_0.1 config.

findings.title: README step 2 runs a script that does not exist
findings.claim: README 'How to use' step 2 instructs `python detection_binoculars_only.py`, but no such file exists in the repo; the actual Binoculars entry point is the `--binoculars_only` flag on detection.py (detection.py:94,113-115).
findings.concern: A user following the README verbatim to reproduce the Binoculars row hits 'No such file or directory'.
findings.resolution: Replace the command with `python detection.py --binoculars_only` (add `--prompt` for white-box), or add the referenced script.
findings.reason: README.md:32 quote matches exactly; detection_binoculars_only.py confirmed absent from repo; detection.py:94,113-115 confirm --binoculars_only flag is the real entry point.

findings.title: prompt_label = idx overwrites the label-conditional; white-box prompts every human text and over-indexes AI texts
findings.claim: In the eval loop over all_texts = human_texts + ai_texts, the intended mapping (init -1 → human text gets NO prompt; AI text at idx gets prompt_list[idx - len(human_texts)]) is destroyed: line 984 unconditionally sets prompt_label = idx, making line 983 dead code. detect() then takes the `prompt_label >= 0` branch for every item.
findings.concern: Contra paper §4.2/Fig.4 ('For human-generated text, only x is input'), every human text is scored WITH a prepended prompt; and each AI text (idx = 200..399) indexes prompt_list at 200..399 instead of 0..199 — for the paper's 200+200 config with a 200-row prompt list this is out of range, so `python detection.py --prompt` raises IndexError at the first AI text (idx=200). The white-box column (the paper's headline result) cannot be produced by this code as written, and where it does not crash it uses the wrong prompt for both classes.
findings.resolution: Guard the override (e.g. `else: prompt_label = -1`) so human texts stay unprompted and AI texts map to prompt_list[idx - len(human_texts)]; confirm which code state produced the committed white-box results.
findings.reason: detector.py:980-985 quote matches exactly; detect() at detector.py:470-471 confirms prompt_label>=0 prepends a prompt; simulation confirms all 200 human texts wrongly get prompted and AI texts (idx 200-399) index prompt_list out of range (len=200) causing IndexError -- the bug is real and independently verifiable in the code logic even though the missing-xsum-ai-dataset issue would surface first at runtime.

findings.title: evaluation.py has an unclosed call and cannot be imported or run
findings.claim: Line 26 opens `random.sample(list(...))` but never closes the sample() call (missing `, size)`), so the module raises SyntaxError: '(' was never closed at line 26 (confirmed by ast.parse over all repo .py files).
findings.concern: The BERTScore prompt-estimation evaluation script is dead on arrival — it cannot be executed to reproduce any prompt-similarity analysis; it also reads two `xsum_est_prompt_for_summary_*` files that are not in txtdata/, and its dependency `evaluate` is absent from requirements.txt.
findings.resolution: Fix the call to `random.sample(list(human_prompt_texts.values()), size)`; add `evaluate`/`bert_score` to requirements and ship the input files (or a fetch).
findings.reason: evaluation.py:25-26 quote matches exactly; ast.parse confirms SyntaxError: '(' was never closed at line 26; requirements.txt confirmed to lack 'evaluate'/'bert_score'; xsum_est_prompt_for_summary_* files confirmed absent from txtdata/.

findings.title: get_roc_metrics compares TPR against FPR targets when picking thresholds
findings.claim: The loop iterates over FPR targets (0.01…0.25) but passes `tpr` (not `fpr`) to find_max_index, so `thresholds_dict[fpr_rate]` is the threshold at the largest index where TPR ≤ fpr_rate — an operating point defined on the wrong ROC axis.
findings.concern: Any TPR@low-FPR operating point read from the saved `threshold` field is computed against TPR instead of FPR and is therefore wrong; the reported ROC-AUC itself is unaffected because it uses auc(fpr, tpr).
findings.resolution: Pass `fpr` to find_max_index (`find_max_index(fpr, fpr_rate)`) so the threshold is chosen at the target false-positive rate.
findings.paper_ref: Section 6 (discussion of high TPR at low FPR)
findings.reason: utils.py:61-66 quote matches exactly; find_max_index(tpr, fpr_rate) is confirmed passing tpr against fpr targets, and roc_auc = auc(fpr, tpr) confirms the AUC itself is computed on the correct axis and unaffected, exactly as claimed.

findings.title: Committed results/*.json do not reproduce Table 2; Entropy/Rank/Log-Rank white-box AUC ≈ 1 − paper
findings.claim: Recomputing ROC-AUC from the repo's own committed results (and matching the stored roc_auc): Entropy WB=0.022, Rank WB=0.023, Log-Rank WB=0.001 — each ≈ (1 − Table 2 value) of 0.978/0.977/0.999; several black-box cells also differ (LRR 0.532→0.406, NPR 0.560→0.679, Entropy 0.330→0.672, Rank 0.432→0.568) and DetectGPT/NPR white-box differ (1.000→0.934, 0.934→0.819).
findings.concern: The committed artefacts contradict Table 2 and, taken at face value, refute the abstract's 'increase in AUC of at least 0.1 across all detectors' for Entropy/Rank/Log-Rank (their committed white-box AUC is far below black-box). Either the paper's Table 2 or these committed results are wrong; the white-box flips are consistent with the prompt-handling bug (see whitebox-prompt-label-overwrite), while the black-box mismatches indicate the shipped results are from a different code/config than Table 2.
findings.resolution: State which commit and command produced Table 2, commit those exact result JSONs, and reconcile the Entropy/Rank/Log-Rank white-box sign convention (the AUC≈1−paper pattern) against the reported values.
findings.reason: Re-ran check_results_vs_table2.py against the committed results/*.json; recomputed numbers match the finding exactly (Entropy WB=0.022, Rank WB=0.023, Log-Rank WB=0.001, LRR BB 0.406, NPR BB 0.679/WB 0.819, Entropy BB 0.672, Rank BB 0.568, DetectGPT WB 0.934); csv row 6 quote matches byte-for-byte; PAPER dict values cross-checked against paper_text.txt Table 2 and match exactly.

findings.title: Binoculars uses OpenLLaMA-3B-v2, not the paper's Phi-1.5 (nor Falcon)
findings.claim: Detector.__init__ reassigns the Binoculars observer/performer three times; the last assignment wins, so the models actually loaded are openlm-research/open_llama_3b_v2 and mediocredev/open-llama-3b-v2-instruct — not the Phi-1.5 pair the paper names, and not the Falcon pair (the class default at detector.py:217-218).
findings.concern: Binoculars is a headline detector in Table 2 (0.877 / 0.999); its reported numbers depend on the specific base/instruct model pair, and the code silently uses a different one than the paper states, so the Binoculars rows are not reproduced with the described configuration.
findings.resolution: Either use the paper's Phi-1.5 pair or update §5.1 to state OpenLLaMA-3B-v2; remove the dead Falcon/Yi assignments to make the intended model unambiguous.
findings.paper_ref: Section 5.1: 'Binoculars employs the pre-trained and instruct-tuned Phi1.5 [27] instead of Falcon.'
findings.reason: detector.py:437-441 quote matches exactly; confirmed the open_llama_3b_v2 pair is the final assignment used in the Binoculars() constructor call at detector.py:443-446 (Falcon default and Yi-6B are dead-assigned); paper_text.txt:558-559 confirms the paper states Phi1.5.

findings.title: Human (short XSum reference summaries) vs AI (≤200-token) texts differ systematically in length
findings.quote:
train_data = batch["document"][0]
if len(train_data) < 1000 or len(train_data) >= 1500:
    continue
human_txts[counter] = batch["summary"][0]
context_txts[counter] = train_data
findings.claim: The human class is the XSum reference summary (batch['summary'], a single sentence; measured median 121 / mean 123 chars over the 200 shipped human samples), while the AI class is Llama-2 output generated with max_new_tokens=200 (generate_ai_dataset.py:58,77). The document (not the human summary) is length-filtered to 1000–1500 chars.
findings.concern: Likelihood/rank/entropy-based scores are strongly length-dependent; if AI texts are several times longer than the one-sentence human summaries, detectors (and the black-box vs white-box gap) may be exploiting a length/format shortcut rather than the prompt effect the paper attributes the gap to.
findings.resolution: Report and match the token-length distributions of the human vs AI classes (or add a length-controlled / length-only baseline); ship the AI summaries so the gap can be quantified — it cannot be measured now because xsum_from_ai_llama2_200.json is absent (see missing-xsum-ai-dataset).
findings.paper_ref: Section 5.1 (200 XSum human samples; Llama2 up to 200 tokens)
findings.reason: generate_human_dataset.py:26-30 quote matches exactly, confirming human class = single-sentence XSum summary and length filter (1000-1500 chars) applies to the document, not the summary; check_data_present.py confirms xsum_human.json median=121/mean=123 chars exactly as claimed; generate_ai_dataset.py:58,77 confirm max_new_tokens default=200 for the AI class. Status/confidence (question/low) already appropriately hedged since the AI-side lengths can't be measured (file absent).
